The two IRW table names are swapped. Checked against the data rather than taken on the paper's say-so: recomputing Cronbach's alpha per letter block on the study's own S1 File reproduces all six of Table 3's published alphas to 3dp (A .807/.8075, B .779/.7789, C .712/.7119, D .743/.7433, E .934/.9335, F .849/.8491; largest deviation .0005), so this table's E block IS the .934 'Consumption intention' factor and misses the .849 'Customer perceived value' factor by .085. Per the Step 3b rule the extraction follows the live data: item_text is the consumption-intention wording and the `instrument` field reads Consumption intention. RECOMMENDED FIX: swap the two table names (or at minimum correct both dictionary Descriptions) in metadata -- the dictionary currently describes this table as a '3-item Customer Perceived Value scale'. The sibling yang_2023_consumption_intent (batch_234) carries the same defect in mirror image and logged the same recommendation; yang_2023_green_brand_image belongs to another agent in this round and was not touched. (2) CODE DERIVATION: the IRW code IS the source column name -- the script's SCALES dict lists the literal strings 'E1','E2','E3' and melts with var_name='item'. No positional step, no rename. (3) mapping_basis=paper_explicit, not data_labels: the S1 File is a plain CSV whose header carries bare codes and no wording at any level (no variable or value labels exist), so the words come from Table 1, which prints each item beside the very code the data uses. Verification is PARTIAL -- see verify_yang_2023_perceived_value.R. (4) TABLE 1 IS AN IMAGE ONLY: no text/HTML endpoint exists and grep for 'E1' over the scraped article returns 0 hits, so item_text is an OCR transcription from the PNG and is worth a human spot-check. Transcribed character by character, including the source's own inconsistencies: E1 and E2 end in a full stop, and E3 ends mid-phrase with no terminal punctuation -- 'I would like to learn about the brand's green agriculture products information and knowledge of'. That dangling 'of' is the paper's own wording and was NOT repaired. (5) LANGUAGE / FALLBACK: administered in Chinese (341 consumers of green agricultural products across China). No Chinese wording exists in scope -- the article has exactly ONE supporting file ('S1 File. Data. ... (CSV)') and it is pure ASCII, zero non-ASCII bytes, no questionnaire supplement. So the 2026-09-01 fallback applies: the study's own English from Table 1 sits in the base fields, the four _translated columns are empty, language=Chinese, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. (6) OPTION TEXT: only the endpoints are labelled anywhere in the paper -- 'The questionnaires were distributed online and offline and scored on a 5-point Likert scale ... That is, 1 means "disagree," and 5 means "agree".' So resp 1='disagree', resp 5='agree', and resp 2/3/4 are left BLANK rather than padded with their own numbers. These are the paper's English methods-section gloss of the administered Chinese anchors, not a printed response scale. (7) instructions and section_prompt are blank: the paper describes the administration but never quotes an instruction stem addressed to respondents, and none was invented. section_id is the trivial yang_2023_perceived_value_1; correct_response is blank throughout (attitude scale, no key). (8) RIGHTS: no block. The three items are the study's own composite adapted from cited marketing literature, not verbatim wording from any named publisher instrument, and they are printed in full in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article. No fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause could be located or quoted for this wording, and no row of itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv applies. Shipped under 'silence is permission'; per the standing rule a round may not write a ship row, so no register row was added. (9) SOURCE DEFECTS recorded so nobody re-derives them: Table 1 prints the third social-image item as C3 while the raw file's column is C4, and Table 4's descriptive rows are shifted relative to their construct labels -- Table 4 was therefore NOT used as evidence. Tables 1 and 3 agree with each other and with the data. Retry test: N/A, this is not a block; the table shipped.
